name: VL53L0X time-of-flight laser distance sensor
description: ST time-of-flight sensor that uses a 940 nm VCSEL laser to measure absolute distance up to about 2 m, read over I2C (up to 400 kHz) at address 0x29. The bare chip runs from 2.6–3.5 V. Common breakouts have a regulator, so they take 2.6–5 V on VIN. Sold as: GY-530 / GY-VL53L0XV2 breakout (6-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, GPIO1, XSHUT) with on-board 2.8 V regulator and level shifting.
eli5: It fires a tiny invisible laser and times how long the light takes to bounce back, which tells you how far away something is in millimetres.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply input, 2.6–5 V on regulated breakouts (3.3 V recommended)

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.description: Open-drain interrupt output that goes active-low when a measurement is ready

pins.name: XSHUT
pins.description: Shutdown input, active low. It is pulled up on the board. Drive it low to hold the sensor in hardware standby, which lets you give several sensors different addresses

supplierQuery: VL53L0X GY-530 time of flight distance sensor breakout
buildNotes: Peel off the protective film (often yellow or orange) over the optical window before using the sensor. If you leave it on, readings will be wrong.
Every VL53L0X starts at address 0x29. To use several on one bus, hold each one's XSHUT low, release them one at a time and write a new address to register 0x8A.
Readings of 8190 or 8191 mm mean the sensor saw no target or is out of range. Expect about 1.2 m indoors in default mode and less in sunlight.
Ranging draws peaks of about 19 mA or more. Put a 10 µF capacitor near VIN if your supply is long or noisy.
Keep fingerprints and dust off the window. A cover glass needs a crosstalk calibration.

# Minimal MicroPython driver for the ST VL53L0X time-of-flight sensor.
# ST does not publish a register map (it ships a C API). This init sequence
# follows the widely used Pololu port of that API.
import time
from micropython import const

_SYSRANGE_START = const(0x00)
_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG = const(0x01)
_SYS_INT_CONFIG_GPIO = const(0x0A)
_SYS_INT_CLEAR = const(0x0B)
_RESULT_INT_STATUS = const(0x13)
_RESULT_RANGE = const(0x1E)   # RESULT_RANGE_STATUS (0x14) + 10
_MSRC_CONFIG = const(0x60)
_SIG_RATE_LIMIT = const(0x44)
_GPIO_HV_MUX = const(0x84)
_VHV_PAD = const(0x89)
_SPAD_REF_0 = const(0xB0)
_ID_MODEL = const(0xC0)
_I2C_ADDR_REG = const(0x8A)

_TUNING = bytes((
 0xFF,0x01, 0x00,0x00, 0xFF,0x00, 0x09,0x00, 0x10,0x00, 0x11,0x00,
 0x24,0x01, 0x25,0xFF, 0x75,0x00, 0xFF,0x01, 0x4E,0x2C, 0x48,0x00,
 0x30,0x20, 0xFF,0x00, 0x30,0x09, 0x54,0x00, 0x31,0x04, 0x32,0x03,
 0x40,0x83, 0x46,0x25, 0x60,0x00, 0x27,0x00, 0x50,0x06, 0x51,0x00,
 0x52,0x96, 0x56,0x08, 0x57,0x30, 0x61,0x00, 0x62,0x00, 0x64,0x00,
 0x65,0x00, 0x66,0xA0, 0xFF,0x01, 0x22,0x32, 0x47,0x14, 0x49,0xFF,
 0x4A,0x00, 0xFF,0x00, 0x7A,0x0A, 0x7B,0x00, 0x78,0x21, 0xFF,0x01,
 0x23,0x34, 0x42,0x00, 0x44,0xFF, 0x45,0x26, 0x46,0x05, 0x40,0x40,
 0x0E,0x06, 0x20,0x1A, 0x43,0x40, 0xFF,0x00, 0x34,0x03, 0x35,0x44,
 0xFF,0x01, 0x31,0x04, 0x4B,0x09, 0x4C,0x05, 0x4D,0x04, 0xFF,0x00,
 0x44,0x00, 0x45,0x20, 0x47,0x08, 0x48,0x28, 0x67,0x00, 0x70,0x04,
 0x71,0x01, 0x72,0xFE, 0x76,0x00, 0x77,0x00, 0xFF,0x01, 0x0D,0x01,
 0xFF,0x00, 0x80,0x01, 0x01,0xF8, 0xFF,0x01, 0x8E,0x01, 0x00,0x01,
 0xFF,0x00, 0x80,0x00))


class VL53L0X:
    def __init__(self, i2c, address=0x29, io_2v8=True, timeout_ms=500):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = address
        self.timeout_ms = timeout_ms
        if bytes(self._rn(_ID_MODEL, 1)) != b'\xee':
            raise OSError('VL53L0X not found (ID reg 0xC0 != 0xEE)')
        self._init(io_2v8)

    # ---- low level ----
    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes((val & 0xFF,)))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _rn(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _r16(self, reg):
        b = self._rn(reg, 2)
        return (b[0] << 8) | b[1]

    def _w16(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes(((val >> 8) & 0xFF, val & 0xFF)))

    def _wait(self, cond):
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not cond():
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > self.timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('VL53L0X timeout')

    # ---- init ----
    def _init(self, io_2v8):
        w, r = self._w, self._r
        if io_2v8:
            w(_VHV_PAD, r(_VHV_PAD) | 0x01)
        w(0x88, 0x00)  # I2C standard mode
        w(0x80, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x00, 0x00)
        self._stop = r(0x91)
        w(0x00, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x00); w(0x80, 0x00)
        w(_MSRC_CONFIG, r(_MSRC_CONFIG) | 0x12)
        self._w16(_SIG_RATE_LIMIT, int(0.25 * 128))  # 0.25 MCPS, Q9.7
        w(_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG, 0xFF)
        # SPAD info
        w(0x80, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x00, 0x00)
        w(0xFF, 0x06); w(0x83, r(0x83) | 0x04); w(0xFF, 0x07); w(0x81, 0x01)
        w(0x80, 0x01); w(0x94, 0x6B); w(0x83, 0x00)
        self._wait(lambda: r(0x83) != 0x00)
        w(0x83, 0x01)
        tmp = r(0x92)
        count = tmp & 0x7F
        aperture = (tmp >> 7) & 0x01
        w(0x81, 0x00); w(0xFF, 0x06); w(0x83, r(0x83) & ~0x04)
        w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x00, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x00); w(0x80, 0x00)
        # reference SPAD map
        ref = bytearray(self._rn(_SPAD_REF_0, 6))
        w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x4F, 0x00); w(0x4E, 0x2C); w(0xFF, 0x00); w(0xB6, 0xB4)
        first = 12 if aperture else 0
        enabled = 0
        for i in range(48):
            if i < first or enabled == count:
                ref[i // 8] &= ~(1 << (i % 8))
            elif (ref[i // 8] >> (i % 8)) & 1:
                enabled += 1
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _SPAD_REF_0, ref)
        # default tuning
        for i in range(0, len(_TUNING), 2):
            w(_TUNING[i], _TUNING[i + 1])
        # interrupt: new sample ready, active low
        w(_SYS_INT_CONFIG_GPIO, 0x04)
        w(_GPIO_HV_MUX, r(_GPIO_HV_MUX) & ~0x10)
        w(_SYS_INT_CLEAR, 0x01)
        w(_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG, 0xE8)
        # reference calibrations
        w(_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG, 0x01); self._ref_cal(0x40)
        w(_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG, 0x02); self._ref_cal(0x00)
        w(_SYS_SEQ_CONFIG, 0xE8)

    def _ref_cal(self, vhv):
        self._w(_SYSRANGE_START, 0x01 | vhv)
        self._wait(lambda: self._r(_RESULT_INT_STATUS) & 0x07)
        self._w(_SYS_INT_CLEAR, 0x01)
        self._w(_SYSRANGE_START, 0x00)

    def _restore_stop(self):
        w = self._w
        w(0x80, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x00, 0x00)
        w(0x91, self._stop)
        w(0x00, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x00); w(0x80, 0x00)

    # ---- public API ----
    def read(self):
        """Single-shot measurement. Returns distance in mm (8190/8191 = out of range)."""
        self._restore_stop()
        self._w(_SYSRANGE_START, 0x01)
        self._wait(lambda: not (self._r(_SYSRANGE_START) & 0x01))
        return self._read_result()

    def _read_result(self):
        self._wait(lambda: self._r(_RESULT_INT_STATUS) & 0x07)
        mm = self._r16(_RESULT_RANGE)
        self._w(_SYS_INT_CLEAR, 0x01)
        return mm

    def start_continuous(self):
        self._restore_stop()
        self._w(_SYSRANGE_START, 0x02)  # back-to-back mode

    def read_continuous(self):
        return self._read_result()

    def stop_continuous(self):
        w = self._w
        w(_SYSRANGE_START, 0x01)
        w(0xFF, 0x01); w(0x00, 0x00); w(0x91, 0x00); w(0x00, 0x01); w(0xFF, 0x00)

    def set_address(self, new_addr):
        self._w(_I2C_ADDR_REG, new_addr & 0x7F)
        self.addr = new_addr

# VL53L0X time-of-flight laser distance sensor (VL53L0X)

## Overview
The **VL53L0X** from STMicroelectronics is a FlightSense time-of-flight ranging sensor. It sends out 940 nm infrared laser pulses (Class 1, eye-safe) and times how long the reflections take to come back. This gives an absolute distance in millimetres, and the result does not depend on the target's colour or reflectance.
- Typical range: up to about 1.2 m in default mode and about 2 m in long-range mode, depending on lighting and the target.
- Each measurement takes about 30 ms with the default timing budget.
- Hobbyists usually buy it on the **GY-530 / GY-VL53L0XV2** breakout (Pololu and Adafruit make similar boards). These boards have a 2.8 V LDO, I2C level shifting and pull-ups.

## Pinout (GY-530 breakout)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | 2.6–5 V supply (3.3 V recommended) |
| GND | Ground |
| SCL | I2C clock |
| SDA | I2C data |
| GPIO1 | Interrupt output, open-drain, active-low when data is ready |
| XSHUT | Shutdown input, active-low, pulled up on the board |

## Electrical limits
- Bare chip AVDD: 2.6–3.5 V (datasheet). Breakout VIN: about 2.6–5 V through the on-board regulator.
- Current: about 19 mA on average while ranging and about 5 µA in hardware standby (XSHUT low). Peak current is higher, so add a 10 µF bulk capacitor.
- I2C: up to 400 kHz.
- Operating temperature: −20 to +70 °C.

## Interface details
- **I2C address: 0x29** (7-bit; the datasheet gives 0x52 as the 8-bit write address). You can change it in software through register **0x8A**, but the change is lost at power-down.
- Identification registers: **0xC0 = 0xEE** (model ID), 0xC1 = 0xAA, 0xC2 = 0x10.
- ST does **not** publish a full register map. The official driver is the C "VL53L0X API" (STSW-IMG005). The driver here follows the open-source Pololu port of that API. Registers it uses:
  - 0x00 SYSRANGE_START: 0x01 = single shot, 0x02 = continuous.
  - 0x13 RESULT_INTERRUPT_STATUS: bits 2:0 are non-zero when data is ready.
  - 0x1E (RESULT_RANGE_STATUS + 10): 16-bit big-endian range in mm.
  - 0x0B SYSTEM_INTERRUPT_CLEAR: write 0x01 after reading.
  - 0x44: signal rate limit, 16-bit value in Q9.7 format (default 0.25 MCPS).
- Out-of-range readings return **8190 or 8191**.

## Wiring
| Breakout | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VIN | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) pin 36 | 3.3 V pin 1 |
| GND | GND | GND pin 38 | GND pin 6 |
| SDA | GPIO21 | GP4 (pin 6) | GPIO2 SDA pin 3 |
| SCL | GPIO22 | GP5 (pin 7) | GPIO3 SCL pin 5 |
| XSHUT | optional GPIO | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |
| GPIO1 | optional GPIO (IRQ) | optional GPIO | optional GPIO |

On the Raspberry Pi 4 with Linux, use the `adafruit-circuitpython-vl53l0x` library instead of the MicroPython driver.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from vl53l0x import VL53L0X

i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(4), scl=Pin(5), freq=400000)   # Pico
tof = VL53L0X(i2c)
while True:
    mm = tof.read()
    print('out of range' if mm >= 8190 else '%d mm' % mm)
    time.sleep_ms(100)
```
For faster streaming, call `tof.start_continuous()` once and then call `tof.read_continuous()` in a loop.

**Several sensors on one bus:**
1. Hold all XSHUT pins low.
2. Release one sensor, create a `VL53L0X(i2c)` object for it and call `set_address(0x30)`.
3. Release the next sensor and give it a different address. Repeat for the rest.

## Gotchas
- **Remove the protective film** from the sensor window before use.
- The address resets to 0x29 on every power cycle or XSHUT reset.
- This simplified driver keeps the default timing budget (about 33 ms) and does not do offset or crosstalk calibration. Expect accuracy of a few percent, with the worst results on very close targets (under 3 cm) or very dark ones.
- Strong sunlight or infrared light shortens the range a lot.
- The field of view is about 25°, so a wide cone may "see" the table or nearby walls.
- If you use the bare chip without a regulator, never give it more than 3.5 V.
- `io_2v8=True` sets the chip's I/O to 2.8 V mode, which matches typical breakouts. Use False only if you drive the bare chip's I/O at 1.8 V.
